paragraphs: Aquarius Spectrum sells acoustic leak detection systems that let water utilities find and prevent leaks. The stated aim is cutting non-revenue water and putting resources where they matter. The products are meant to suit water networks of any pipe material and size.

Sensors take a daily audio sample and send it to a cloud server for analysis. Every two coupled sensors are then correlated, and when the same noise turns up in the same location an alert gives the exact position of the leak. The AQS-SYS platform pairs those sensors with algorithms, big data analytics and CAT-M or NB-IoT connectivity. Accelerometers fit externally on hydrants above ground and on pressure and air valves below. A hydrophone covers large transmission lines of 24 inches and above, plus plastic and PVC pipe. Where continuous monitoring is not wanted, mobile products let a utility survey large areas instead.

Alongside the hardware the company sells what it calls Human-as-a-Service, described as ongoing human support, expertise and system updates. AQS states that it is a company of the Aliaxis Group. It reports receiving ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification. Published case studies include the national agency that manages Singapore's water loop.
